title: Review of c46's hunting-ecology claim on fresh seed 4 (256^2, with the X twin and the E fork): predators crash the prey and divide after meals, the predator-free twin is a static growing emulsion, and a fuel cut dissolves every prey body; prey themselves barely divide and predators are short-lived
summary: The claim's world.py unchanged, labkit 256^2, seed 4, t=12000, --lineage-k 5. Prey form from noise (56 by t=2000); predators added at t=2000 take them to 7 by t=3000, prey regrow to 66 by t~5700 and fall again to 18-28, while predators rise 58 -> 82 and hold 69-76 (metrics.json species n_comp): one lagged predator-prey swing, not repeated cycles, within 12000 t. Predator persistent splits 21, generation 2; the claim's strict test splits3.py with min area 10 finds 15 predator divisions (8 near prey), and strict_pred_s4_a10.png shows predators cutting into prey, elongating and pinching into pieces (t=7000-10000). With the claim's default area 30 it finds 2. Prey: 4 persistent splits, generation 1, 1 strict division. Predator-free twin (pred_on 0, same seed and grid): 87 static prey at the end, generation 1, 1 moving track. Fuel fork at t=6000 (128^2, seed 4, drive.py): prey 11 -> 0 by t=6500 and max prey field 0.91 -> 0.48 -> 0.29 while prey material stays 0.21 -> 0.18; the fed twin keeps 2-6 prey bodies with max 0.69-0.91 (predators are eating them too).

observations.I: pack256/seed4/sheet.png: discrete prey droplets and predator droplets; prey tracks persist hundreds of t, predators dim between meals (1 persistent predator track)

observations.D: predator persistent splits 21 (generation 2); strict_pred_s4_a10.png: 15 strict predator divisions after meals
observations.E: efork/fork_s4.json: prey 11 -> 0 within 500 t of the fuel cut, max prey 0.91 -> 0.29, prey material kept; fed twin max 0.69-0.91

seeds_run.result: pass for X, predator D and prey E; prey D thin (1 strict division), one lagged swing rather than repeated cycles

controls_run.X: twin256/seed4 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, lineage window)

verdicts.limitation: D is the predators' and E is the prey's, so no single kind shows I, D and E together; the prey divide rarely with predators present (4 persistent, 1 strict). Predator division counts depend on the strict test's minimum area (15 at 10 px, 8 at 15 px, 2 at the default 30 px). The fork is at 128^2 with drive.py counts, and on this seed the fed twin's prey are also being eaten, so the fork's contrast is in the condensed state (max field), not only in counts. One fresh seed.
